text:
maya.g: quick heads-up — ran a TTL-based KV prune stress on H100 (eu-west-1) against redm-13b-8k q8_0. observed sharp p99 regressions during prune windows, wondering if kernel swap / allocator churn is causing it. repro below

samir: can you paste the exact command + config? and a small excerpt of the logs so we can see kernel/alloc events

maya.g: sure — test command and config:```
./bench_kv --model=redm-13b-8k --quant=q8_0 --region=eu-west-1 --gpu=h100 --seq-dist=mix:20,128,512 --load=120rps --ttl-prune=true --ttl=5s --prune-interval=10s --evict-window=0.25
```

maya.g: log snippet (trimmed):```
[2024-06-18T11:02:12Z] serve: token_gen p50=42ms p95=185ms p99=430ms
[2024-06-18T11:02:20Z] kvcache: prune triggered, reclaiming 18% pages
[2024-06-18T11:02:20Z] runtime: kernel_swap fallback -> generic_attention_kernel
[2024-06-18T11:02:20Z] serve: token_gen p50=65ms p95=260ms p99=498ms
```

jon: jump in — that kernel_swap line is the interesting bit. when pages get invalidated we sometimes fall back to a slower kernel (e.g., generic_attention) while the optimized kernel path re-evaluates supported shapes / memory layout. with mixed seqlen there are more shape variations which can trigger that. can you share quant/kernel mapping?

meera: model & quant: redm-13b-8k q8_0 (channel-optimized kernels). eviction_window=0.25 means aggressive reclaim. when TTL prune runs it effectively bulk-invalidates prefixes which floods the prefetch/warmup window. we saw hitrate drop from ~72% -> ~45% during prune bursts which explains throughput dip.

rishi: raw numbers we captured across regions/gpus:```
H100 eu-west-1 (ttl prune on): p50 48ms p95 220ms p99 430ms throughput 115 rps hitrate 45%
H100 eu-west-1 (ttl prune off / LRU steady): p50 38ms p95 170ms p99 210ms throughput 158 rps hitrate 72%
A100 us-west-2 (ttl prune on): p50 50ms p95 210ms p99 380ms throughput 120 rps hitrate 50%
A100 us-west-2 (ttl prune off): p50 40ms p95 175ms p99 230ms throughput 150 rps hitrate 70%
```

samir: interesting that A100 p99 is slightly better than H100 in prune bursts — likely because our H100 optimized kernel selection path has a more expensive fallback transition when pages change shape. H100 kernels benefit when the cache is warm and shape/profile stable.

jon: actionable checklist: 1) reduce prune aggressiveness (ttl=30s or increase prune-interval) 2) instrument kernel selection events to track fallback rate 3) try pinning kernel variants for the common seqlen buckets (20/128/512) to avoid re-eval on small churn 4) run microbench with synthetic single-seqlen to measure baseline swap cost

meera: quick config I suggest to A/B test:```
kvcache:
  prune:
    mode: ttl
    ttl_seconds: 30
    interval_seconds: 60
    batch_reclaim_pct: 3
  eviction_window: 0.1
  prefetch_warmup: 200ms
```

maya.g: noted. i'll run two confirmatory jobs: (A) ttl less aggressive as above on H100 eu, (B) switch prune->LRU with same memory pressure. planning to run for 2 hours each during low-traffic window.

rishi: also try a quick quant-control: q8_0 vs q4_0_abs (if supported) — lower precision sometimes changes kernel selection and can avoid fallback. might change quality though. run eval set.

infra-bot: scheduled: perf-test job maya.kv-ttl-A (1729876600) and maya.kv-lru-B (1729876605) — results will be posted to #eng-ml when complete.

release-bot: FYI @channel — remember to tag test runs with experiment-id so we can correlate infra logs: exp=kv-ttl-prune-2024-06-18

samir: one more thought — add a small jitter to prune times across machines to avoid synchronized reclaim waves across a region (that amplifies cache miss storm).

maya.g: good call. I'll add jitter and the less-aggressive config, run both H100 & A100, then post summary with kernel selection traces & hitrate curves. thanks all :thumbsup:
